name: Prismveil AR Visor — Chromeline Edition
description: A wide wraparound visor in gradient-tinted polychromatic glass that shifts from deep amber at the top edge to near-clear at the chin. The titanium-alloy frame is brushed silver with exposed screw heads as deliberate design details. Embedded AR overlay projectors sit inside each temple arm, invisible from outside. The nose bridge is adjustable via a magnetic micro-ratchet. Available in a horn-clearance variant with an elevated crown bridge.
functionality: Full AR overlay — navigation, biometric ID scanning, corporate network access, and environmental hazard tagging. Syncs with BCI or standalone via temporal-arm touchpad. UV and light chemical-splash rated. Prescription lens inserts sold separately.
what_it_says: You can afford to see more than everyone else, and you're not hiding that.
story_hooks: A recent firmware update added a passive data-harvest layer that logs everything the wearer looks at for more than 1.2 seconds — Prismveil's terms of service buried the disclosure on page 47.
The horn-clearance variant has become unexpectedly fashionable among non-geneware Tier 4 wearers as a status signal, which is causing tension in geneware communities.
A black-market firmware patch promises to unlock the biometric scanner's full law-enforcement-grade capability; someone is selling it in the Circuit for Φ60 a flash.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, oversized wraparound visor that dominates the upper face with a futuristic, almost insectoid presence. The gradient lens creates a sunset-to-transparent effect that catches light dynamically. Sits low on the bridge, cradling the eyes with a confident, forward-gazing stance. Projects wealth and bleeding-edge access.
physical_description.fit: Form-fitted to the contours of the face via adjustable magnetic bridge; temple arms hug the sides of the head snugly without pressure. Crown bridge elevates slightly above natural hairline for clearance. Lightweight titanium construction means it feels almost weightless once settled.
physical_description.primary_material: Polychromatic gradient-tinted optical glass (amber to clear); brushed titanium-alloy frame; embedded AR projector lenses (sapphire substrate)
physical_description.texture: Glass is smooth and reflective with a subtle gradient visible on close inspection; titanium frame has a matte brushed finish with deliberate exposed screw heads that catch light, adding tactile visual interest
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep burnt amber at top lens edge transitioning to pale honey-gold at midpoint, then fading to nearly colorless at chin. Frame is brushed silver-grey with darker anodized accents around the screw heads.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic micro-ratchet adjustment on the nose bridge; temple arms curve around the ears with passive friction-fit retention
distinctive_features: Wide wraparound polychromatic gradient lens that shifts color with viewing angle
Exposed titanium screw heads as intentional design flourish
Invisible embedded AR overlay projectors in temple arms
Adjustable nose bridge via magnetic ratchet system
Horn-clearance variant with elevated crown bridge for non-standard head geometries
Sapphire-substrate AR emitters that hint at internal complexity
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury; cutting-edge corpo consumer tech at premium price point (estimated 8,500-12,000 Φ)
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals early adopter status, corpo affiliation, or high-earning independent. Wearing this announces access to exclusive AR overlays and corpo networks. Often seen on executives, corpo security, and wealthy independents in the GLMZ commercial districts.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine; these visors are maintained obsessively by owners. Occasional micro-scratches on lens from environmental exposure, but the gradient hides minor imperfections. Frame stays buffed and screw heads polished.

image_prompt: Close-up fashion photograph of the Prismveil Chromeline AR Visor worn by a sharp-featured neo-noir model with subtle facial augmentations (faint chrome cheekbone implants, bioluminescent iris). The visor's gradient lens catches neon amber and blue ambient light, reflecting the glow. Brushed titanium frame gleams under moody, high-contrast studio lighting. Urban backdrop: rain-wet mega-structure, holographic advertisements bleeding through wet pavement reflections. Shallow depth of field emphasizes the visor's optical complexity and the wearer's focused, augmented gaze. Cosmopolitan, aspirational. --ar 2:3 --v 6
